chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all together, from Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, who said:

I and the Shaykh Abu 'Amr, may God have mercy on him, gathered in the presence of Ahmad ibn Ishaq. Ahmad ibn Ishaq nudged me to ask him about the Successor (the hidden Imam). So I said to him: 'O Abu 'Amr! I want to ask you about something, and I have no doubt regarding what I want to ask you. My belief and my religion is that the earth cannot be devoid of a Divine Proof (Hujja) — except when it is forty days before the Day of Resurrection. When that occurs, the Proof will be lifted and the door of repentance will be closed, such that no soul's faith shall benefit it if it had not believed before, nor if it had earned good through its faith.'

'Those would be the most wicked of God's creation, Mighty and Majestic, and they are those upon whom the Resurrection shall occur. However, I wished to increase in certainty, just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to show him how He revives the dead. He said: Do you not believe? He said: Yes, but so that my heart may be at peace.'

'And Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ishaq informed me from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying: I asked him and said: With whom shall I deal, or from whom shall I take, and whose word shall I accept? So he said to him: Al-'Amri is my trusted one. Whatever he conveys to you from me, he conveys from me, and whatever he says to you from me, he says from me. Listen to him and obey, for he is the trustworthy, the reliable.'

'And Abu Ali informed me that he asked Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the same, and he said to him: Al-'Amri and his son are both trustworthy. Whatever they both convey to you from me, they convey from me, and whatever they both say to you, they say from me. Listen to them both and obey them, for they are both trustworthy and reliable. This is the word of two Imams, both of whom have passed, regarding you.'

He said: Abu 'Amr then fell prostrate and wept. Then he said: 'Ask your need.' I said to him: 'You have seen the Successor from after Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'Yes, by God, and his neck was like this,' and he gestured with his hand.

I said to him: 'There remains one (question).' He said to me: 'Go ahead.' I said: 'The name?' He said: 'It is forbidden for you to ask about that, and I do not say this from myself — it is not for me to permit or forbid — but it is from him (peace be upon him). For the matter with the ruling authority is that Abu Muhammad passed away and left no son, his inheritance was divided and was taken by those with no right to it, and now his household is roaming about — no one dares to introduce himself to them or give them anything. If the name were to occur, the pursuit would occur — so fear God and refrain from that.'

Al-Kulayni, may God have mercy on him, said: A shaykh from among our companions, whose name escapes me, narrated to me that Abu 'Amr was asked by Ahmad ibn Ishaq about the same matter, and he answered with the same.

key_terms.الثِّقَةُ الْمَأْمُونُ: The trustworthy, the reliable — the double endorsement given by the Imams to authenticate the deputies' authority
key_terms.السُّلْطَان: The ruling authority — referring to the 'Abbasid caliphate, which was persecuting the Imam's household and searching for his heir
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: The Divine Proof/Authority — a title for the Imam as God's proof (hujja) on earth, whose presence is necessary to maintain the world
key_terms.الْخَلَف: The Successor — a title used for the hidden Imam al-Mahdi, meaning the one who succeeds (khalafa) the previous Imam
key_terms.الْعَمْرِيُّ: Al-'Amri — referring to 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-'Askari (Abu 'Amr) and his son Muhammad ibn 'Uthman, the first and second deputies of Imam al-Mahdi

ai.seo_question: Who confirmed seeing Imam al-Mahdi during the Minor Occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith records a pivotal encounter during the Minor Occultation (al-Ghayba al-Sughra, 260-329 AH) between the scholar Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari and Abu 'Amr 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-'Askari, the first of the Four Deputies of Imam al-Mahdi. Al-Himyari, prompted by Ahmad ibn Ishaq, questions Abu 'Amr about having personally witnessed the hidden Imam. Abu 'Amr confirms he saw the twelfth Imam while presenting Imamic endorsements from both al-Hadi and al-'Askari authorizing the deputyship of the 'Amri family. He then refuses to reveal the Imam's name, explaining this prohibition came directly from the Imam himself, due to the dangerous political climate under 'Abbasid rule, which was actively searching for the Imam's heir. The hadith authenticates the deputyship system and the doctrine of al-Ghayba through first-hand testimony.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abdullah and Muhammad Bin Yahya, altogether from Abdullah Bin Ja’far Al Humeyri who said,

‘I and Sheykh Abu Amro, may Allahazwj be Pleased with him, gathered in the presence of Ahmad Bin Is’haq. So Ahmad Bin Is’haq winked at me that I should ask him about the replacement (Imamasws). So I said to him, ‘O Abu Amro! I want to ask you about something, and I am not with a doubt regarding what I intend to ask you about. So my belief and my Religion is that the earth cannot be empty from a Divine Authority except when it would be just before the Day of Judgment by forty days. So when it would be that, the Divine Authority would be Raised and the door of repentance would be shut. Thus, no soul shall benefit by its Eman which it did not belief from before, or goodness having been earned by its Eman [6:158] its faith shall not profit a soul, which did not believe before, or earn good through its faith.

So they would be the most evil of the creatures of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, and they are those against whom the Day of Judgment would be Established. But, I would like to increase conviction and that Ibrahimas asked hisas Lordazwj Mighty and Majestic how Heazwj Revives the dead [2:260] He said: Or you do not believe? He said: Yes, but to reassure my heart.

And Abu Ali Ahmad Bin Is’haq informed me from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) saying, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> and said, ‘So who is the office bearer, or from whom should I take, and whose word should I accept?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Al-Amiry is my<sup>asws</sup> reliable one, therefore whatever he brings to you from me<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> have put it across, and whatever he says to you from me<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> have said it. Therefore, listen to him and obey, for he is the reliable, the trustworthy’.

And Abu Ali informed me that he asked Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about similar to that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Al-Amiry and his son are two reliable ones. So whatever they both bring to you from me<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> have put it across to them, and whatever they both say to you, so I<sup>asws</sup> have said it to them. Therefore, listen to them both and obey them, for they are both reliable ones, trustworthy ones. So these are the words of two Imams<sup>asws</sup> proceeding with regards to you’.

He said, ‘So Abu Amro fell prostrating and wept. Then he said, ‘Ask your need’. So I said to him, ‘You have seen the replacement (Imam<sup>asws</sup>) from after Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>?’. So he said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and his<sup>asws</sup> neck was similar to that’, and he gestured by his hand.

So I said to him, ‘So there remains one (question)’. So he said to me, ‘Give’. I said, ‘So (what is) the name?’ He said, ‘It is Prohibited upon you that you should be asking about that nor will I be saying this from myself. Thus, there isn’t for me that I should permit nor that I should prohibit, but it is from him<sup>asws</sup>, for the matter with the ruling authority (Caliph Mu’tasim) is that Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> passed away and did not leave behind a son, and he<sup>asws</sup> distributed his<sup>asws</sup> inheritance, and it was taken by the ones who had no right to it with regards to it, and he<sup>asws</sup> is with dependents who are roaming around. There isn’t anyone bold enough that he should introduce himself to them nor give them anything. And when the name will occur, the seeking (from the ruling authorities) would occur, therefore fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and withhold from that’.

Al-Kulayni, may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on him, said, ‘It was narrated to me by a companions whose name escapes me, that Amro asked from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, about similar to this, so he answered with similar to this’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah and Muhammad ibn Yahya, all have narrated from ‘Abdallah ibn Ja‘far al-Himyari who has said the following.

“I and shaykh abu ‘Amr, may Allah grant him blessings met each other before Ahmad ibn Ishaq. Ahmad ibn Ishaq made an eye gesture to me to ask him about the succeeding Imam. I said to him, “O abu ‘Amr, I like to ask you a question about a matter, although, I do not any doubts in the question I am about to ask. It is my belief and religion that the earth is not left without a Leadership with Divine Authority except if would be just before the coming of the Day of Judgment by forty days because in such a period Leadership with Divine Authority will take away. The door to repentance will be closed. No soul will benefit from the faith with which it has not achieved any good deeds. “. . the belief of any soul will be of no avail to it unless some good deeds have been done with it, or it has been formed before the coming of such a day. .”

[6:158] Such people would be of the evil creatures of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, and it is these people on whom the Day of Judgment will be established. However, I wanted to strengthen my faith further just as Abrahm (a.s.) asked his Lord, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, to show him how would He will bring the dead to life again. He said, “When Abraham prayed, “Lord, show me how you bring the dead back to life,” the Lord said, “Do you not yet believe?” Abraham replied, “I believe but want more confidence for my heart.. .”

[2:260] Abu Ali Ahmad ibn Ishaq has inarrated to me from abu al-Hassan (a.s.) who has said that he asked the Imam (a.s.), “With who should I deal and ask questions about my faith and religion and whose words should I accept (after you)?”

The Imam (a.s.) said to him, “Al-‘Amri is trustworthy to me. Whatever he will deliver to you is from me. From me he delivers. Whatever he would say is from me, from me he saays it. Listen to him and obey him because he is reliable and trustworthy. Abu Ali has said to me that he asked abu Muhammad (a.s.) a similar question and he said to him, “Al-‘Amri and his son are trustworthy people. Whatever they would deliver to you is from me from they deliover. Whatevet they say to you from they say it. Listen to them and obey them because they are trustworthy and reliable people. These are the words of the Imams spoken about you.

Abu ‘Amr fell down on his face in prostration and wept. Then he said, “Ask what you need to ask.” I said, “Did you see the succeeding Imam (Leader with Divine Authority) after abu Muhammad (a.s.) ?” He said, “Yes, by Allah , his neck was like that-making a gesture with his hand.”

I then said, “Onne more question is left.” He said, “Say, whaever is is it.” I said, “What is his (succeding Imam) name?” He said, “It is unlawful for you to ask about it. I do not say this because abu left this world without a surviving son. His legacy is distributed and is taken away by one who has no right in it. He is (that prson). His family is despersed and no one has the courage to learn about them or recieve any thing from them.

When the name is mentioned search for him will take place. Have fear of Allah and abstain from it.” Al-Kulayni, may Allah grant his soul blessings, has said, “:A shaykh from our people narrated this to me – his name I have forgotten- that abu’Amr asked Ahmad ibn Ishaq a similar question and received a similar answer.”
